description_full: EPAM Systems, Inc. provides digital platform engineering and software development services worldwide. The company offers engineering services, including requirements analysis and platform selection, customization, cross-platform migration, implementation, and integration; cloud services for creating a roadmap to set and refine IT and business goals while identifying new and emerging opportunities leveraging cloud technologies; data, analytics, and artificial intelligence; customer experience; marketing; and cybersecurity. It also offers operation solutions comprising integrated engineering practices and smart automation services. In addition, the company offers software product and platform development services, which comprise product research, customer experience design and prototyping, program management, component design and integration, full lifecycle software testing, product deployment and end-user customization, performance tuning, product support and maintenance, managed services, as well as cross-platform migration and modernizing legacy platforms. The company has a collaboration with Wiz to help organizations turn cloud risk intelligence into continuous, AI-powered, and engineering-led remediation across complex multi-cloud environments. The company serves the financial services; consumer goods, retail, and travel; software and hi-tech; business information and media; life sciences and healthcare; and emerging vertical industries. EPAM Systems, Inc. was founded in 1993 and is headquartered in Newtown, Pennsylvania.

financial_summary: EPAM Systems, Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $8.3B market cap on $5.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years and +20% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 28% against a 11% cost of capital — a 18-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $613M in free cash flow — roughly 11 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.73× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 8.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 3.3% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
